attributes.provenance: Fleet worker SH, work_claim.shop-buffer-naming.20260901.v1, commit 518a02789 (declaration, byte-identical) and e88cf5b06 (slot correction). Supersedes v1, whose STRUCTURE half is confirmed and extended and whose NAMES half is refuted.

subject: tu:game/shop/shop
value:
RESOLVED. v1's verdict was 'structure proven, names NOT recoverable, so all ~56 sites stay raw'. The structure half stands and is extended; the NAMES half is REFUTED, and the record is now declared in src/game/shop/shop.c as `ShopPage` (file-local, per the embedded-struct cascade law). The buffer is ONE object of exactly 0x1E00 = 7680 bytes.

WHY v1 CONCLUDED NAMES WERE UNAVAILABLE, AND WHY THAT WAS WRONG. v1 searched the Xbox SHOP.OBJ DATA ROSTER in research/xbox_symbols/functions_by_module.txt, found its ~26 globals were all 4/16/48 bytes, correctly observed that none is large enough to be any of the big GC tables, and stopped. It also reported 'no PDB struct record covers the region (gdlmem struct finds none)'. That second statement is the error: the roster is not the only PDB evidence, and the struct index does hold the record -- it is simply not reachable by searching for a GLOBAL's name, because on Xbox the big region is an array of a TYPE. `gdlmem.py struct player_shop_state` returns size 768 with three 256-byte fields, item_availability_flags at 0, item_sale_value at 256, item_to_player_map at 512. The GC region at +336 has a MEASURED per-player stride of 768 (do_shopping and write_shop_menu both spell `player * 768 + 336`), is 3072 bytes long, and the one field GC reads at sub-offset 0 is a per-item flag word tested with `& 4` -- an availability flag. Size, stride, field count and semantics all agree, so +336 is `player_shop_state st[4]` and the name is adopted from the PDB, not invented. LESSON FOR THE NEXT NAMING BLOCK: when a roster of globals fails, search the STRUCT index by shape (size and stride) before declaring names unavailable; a region that looks nameless as a global may be a named TYPE.

THE FULL LAYOUT, which closes exactly on the three extractor symbol sizes (0xD50 + 0xC00 + 0x4B0 == 0x1E00): 0x0000 cursor_y[4]; 0x0010 top_y[4]; 0x0020 curfreeze[4]; 0x0030 scroll_flag[4]; 0x0040 last_available[4]; 0x0050 pile_targ[4][3]; 0x0080 pile_shown[4][3]; 0x00B0 pile_val[4][3]; 0x00E0 pile_count[4][3]; 0x0110 pad 0x40; 0x0150 player_shop_state st[4]; 0x0D50 item_y[4][64]; 0x1150 avail[4][64]; 0x1550 timers[4][64]; 0x1950 void* item_blits[4][64]; 0x1D50 void* blits[4][6]; 0x1DB0 pad 0x50.

THE SMALL ARRAYS ARE NOW NAMED, AND v1's OWN OBJECTION IS ANSWERED. v1 rejected the five 16-byte and four 48-byte Xbox globals because 'the Xbox ORDER differs from GC's, so the small arrays cannot be assigned one-to-one without a tiebreak'. Order is the wrong tiebreak; ROLE is the right one, and four of the five have directly observable GC roles: top_y (+0x10) is do_shopping's window top; curfreeze (+0x20) is nonzero while the list scrolls and is what do_shopping gates buy/sell input on, reading its value as the scroll speed; scroll_flag (+0x30) is the 0/1 word write_shop_menu clears on entry and sets when the list must move; last_available (+0x40) is the item-count bound the cursor wraps at; cursor_y (+0x00) is set to cursor index minus top. The COUNTS and SHAPES match the Xbox roster exactly (five 16-byte, four 48-byte), so the assignment is a bijection with four independently pinned by behaviour. NOTE the correction inside this pass: curfreeze and scroll_flag were initially assigned the other way round and were swapped once write_shop_menu's `*(scrollflag += 12) = 0` was read -- that site reaches +0x30, not +0x20, which is what pins the 0/1 flag there (commit e88cf5b06). The four 48-byte pile_* arrays keep GC-behavioural names (pile_targ / pile_shown / pile_val / pile_count) because show_gold and fn_8009A0AC pin their ROLES but not which Xbox pile_* spelling belongs to which -- those four remain the only un-adopted names in the record, and they are the honest residual of this claim.

WHAT IS NOT CHANGED. The symbol-separation axis was NOT retried and remains refuted per claim.law.single-base-relocation-refutes-symbol-separation.20260831.v1: lbl_802897D0 stays the sole relocated base for the six consumers that pool it, and calc_shop_ypos keeps its interior-symbol spellings `&lbl_8028A520[player<<6]` / `&lbl_8028B120[player<<6]` (that function is real 0 and was not touched). Declaring the record did NOT require choosing between the two spellings -- both still coexist legitimately in the TU.

WHAT THE DECLARATION BOUGHT, so the next agent does not re-derive it: adopting it is NOT a blanket win. See claim.law.record-respelling-pays-per-region-not-per-population.20260901.v1 -- the conversion pays where one addressing region covers every site (show_piles went to an IDENTICAL opcode multiset, show_gold and fn_8009A0AC improved or held) and costs where sites span several regions (do_shopping and write_shop_menu both regressed fuzzy and were reverted). The single largest free win was retyping the extern itself, worth real 831 -> 826 on do_shopping with no site edits at all.
